bug_semantics: In DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener, HTTP/2 content decompression uses a per-stream EmbeddedChannel whose tail ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter is the sole owner of each pooled decompressed ByteBuf. channelRead calls listener.onDataRead and then connection.local().flowController().consumeBytes before buf.release(). If the flow controller (or onDataRead) throws, release is skipped, leaking one direct ByteBuf per DATA frame. A remote peer can force that throw path and exhaust native/direct memory until JVM OOME.
flaw_origin: 9d804c54ce962408ae6418255a83a13924f7145d (2025-09-03, 4.2 'Merge commit from fork') rewrote HTTP/2 decompression from a pull-loop that released each buf in a try/finally into a push tail-handler that fires chunks immediately. The new handler copied consumeBytes(onDataRead(...)) then buf.release() without the parent finally, so a flow-controller exception became a leak. 4.1 received the same first-write later the same day as squash #15612 (34894ac73b02efefeacd9c0972780b32dc3de04f). Later padding accounting (e7d3b4850e6 / 2387f3217439) only inserted incrementDecompressedBytes(padding) above the already-leaky calls.

reasoning: The advisory is a real, published ByteBuf leak (CVE-2026-48043 / GHSA-c2gf-v879-257j; not withdrawn). Before 2025-09-03 the HTTP/2 decompressor pulled EmbeddedChannel output in a loop and always released the current buf in finally, so a flow-controller throw did not leak. 9d804c54ce962408ae6418255a83a13924f7145d first wrote the push tail-handler that owns each decompressed buf and calls consumeBytes(onDataRead(...)) then release without finally; git log -L/-S and parent-tree inspection show those lines absent at edb55fd8e0a3bcbd85881e423464f585183d1284. That squash from a private security fork cannot be decomposed further in public history, so it is the BIC as the smallest surviving first-write. 4.1 #15612 is a same-day port, not an earlier origin. The 2026-06 fixes restore finally around the same calls and land in the advertised patched tags.
